title: Microsoft Teams: live captions get a right-side panel and one settings menu
summary: Hold: the Teams Premium requirement omits Microsoft's exception for translated captions in large-audience events, which could lead to unnecessary licence purchases. The roadmap facts, automatic rollout and live captions policy controls are supported; smaller corrections concern rollout wording, licensing context and a missing table reference.

claims.claim: Learn's release notes say the live captions profanity filter default changed from On to Off only for users who had never configured their preference.
claims.quote:
We are updating the default profanity filter setting for live captions from On to Off
This change will only affect users who have never configured their live captions profanity filter preference.

claims.claim: Live captions continue to follow each participant's own profanity preference.
claims.quote: Live captions continue to follow each participant’s profanity setting.

claims.claim: The admin profanity policy described in Learn's release notes governs live transcription and saved transcripts, not the participant's live captions profanity setting.
claims.quote: Teams admins can use a meeting policy to control whether profane words are masked in live transcription and saved meeting transcripts. Filtering is on by default. If the meeting organizer is assigned a policy that turns it off, profane words appear unmasked in both transcripts.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The live captions control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Live captions.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
From the drop-down for Live captions, select Not enabled, but users can enable(default value) or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled turns off live captions for users assigned that policy.
claims.quote:
To turn off live captions for users with this policy, run the following script:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -LiveCaptionsEnabledType Disabled

claims.claim: Live captions is a per-user meeting policy controlling whether that user can turn captions on in meetings they attend.
claims.quote: This setting is a per-user policy and applies during a meeting. This setting controls whether the Turn on live captions option is available for the user to turn automatically generated live captions on or off in meetings that the user attends.

claims.claim: The live captions policy defaults to DisabledUserOverride, labelled Not enabled, but users can enable on the cited page.
claims.quote: Not enabled, but users can enable | DisabledUserOverride | This value is the default setting. Live captions are off by default, but users with this assigned policy can turn on live captions during meetings or events.
claims.fix: After the default sentence add: 'The Teams settings and policies reference instead labels the Live captions default "Off, but organizers and co-organizers can turn them on".' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/settings-policies-reference#meetings for that differing label; retain the default parameter value supported by the cited captions page.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Setting Live captions to Off also turns off live translated captions, which otherwise require Not enabled, but users can enable.
claims.quote: To turn on live translated captions, you must set Live captions to Not enabled, but users can enable in the corresponding meeting policy in the Teams admin center. To turn off live translated captions, set Live captions to Off.
